synopsis: PMBOK and PRINCE2 are general project-management methods, while agile comprises practices for delivering work in short, repeated cycles; relevant editions are PMI’s PMBOK Guide 7 (2021) and PeopleCert’s PRINCE2 7 (2023) [f16418, f16420, f16421]. The booklet recommends borrowing their document structure for the validation plan, but labels these sources expert opinion and stresses that neither establishes whether a simulation is trustworthy [f9982, f16424, f16430]. Agile precedents include Cooper’s 2016 Agile-Stage-Gate hybrid and Lockheed Martin’s claim that agile development plus reuse enabled F-35 Auto-GCAS integration in 2019, seven years earlier than planned [f9501, f16422, f1443]. These precedents do not resolve the evidence gap: the booklet found no consistent outcome evidence for any planning method in programs like this one, and none for rolling-wave planning specifically [f16426, f16425]. Its preferred approach layers methods around systems-engineering verification and validation, with knowledge before commitment as the best-supported principle, although its cost and schedule evidence is correlational rather than causal [f16428, f16427].
